source.original_title: 05/16/2026 - Antonio Gatlin & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/16/2026 - Antonio Gatlin & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

prospect.name: Antonio Gatlin II
prospect.occupation: Barber manager at a state prison, teaching inmates barbering — 7:30am to 3:30pm, started four weeks earlier; previously a shop barber working 10am-7pm. Marine Corps veteran, four years. Exploring barbershop ownership with an investor.
prospect.family_status: Engaged; five children, four boys and a girl. Household also includes his mother, his sister and his sister's son.
prospect.training_background: Four years in the Marine Corps where fitness was structural; has struggled to hold a routine since leaving. Somewhat familiar with kettlebells and owns an 8kg bell bought after finding Trevor's Instagram, but cannot build a workout around it. Now up at 4:30am with about an hour before work. Has previously used ChatGPT to try to build a plan.
prospect.medical: Shoulder pain for roughly the last six months, which he attributes to the arms-forward posture of cutting hair plus unbalanced training. He has been assessed: "I've also gone to the, you know, to see my medical providers with the VA and they've had, they haven't found anything through x-rays or anything wrong with it at all." No clinician has cleared him for loaded kettlebell work and the rep did not ask. Self-describes as overweight: "I'm overweight, but I want to lose weight."

signals: Lost a structure he used to have — four years of Marine Corps fitness, then 'it's been a little bit of a challenge adjusting in the civilian world'
Wants the former self back and frames it as overdue: 'I feel that I've reached that point in life where it hurts more to be where I'm at than it does to make a change'
Classic rebuilder cycle rather than an optimiser's plateau: 'I'm gonna do this for like a week or two weeks... and then, you know, life happens... and then I fail'
Not medically constrained — the shoulder was investigated and imaging was clear — and not price-resistant on value, only on capacity

goals.text: Lose a substantial amount of weight over six months
Have the energy to play, bike and be present with his five kids instead of arriving home drained
Build a system so consistency stops depending on willpower
Relieve the shoulder pain and improve mobility and strength
Lead by example for his fiancée, who 'feeds off my energy'
Be physically capable and command respect in a prison environment where he is seen as an instructor and role model
Improve mood and reduce stress so he handles what gets thrown at him better
Pass something down — do the mobility work alongside his kids in the mornings

pains.text: Consistency runs on willpower and collapses after one to two weeks — 'I don't have the system set in place. And then my accountability takes a hit and then I fail'
Comes home completely drained and has to tell his kids 'dad's too tired', with guilt attached
Shoulder pain for around six months, attributed to barbering posture, investigated by the VA with no findings
Overweight and wants to lose weight
Cannot structure a workout around the kettlebell he already owns
Nine-person household with shared cooking and one fridge — no room for a single diet plan, and comes home to his mother's cooking when he is weakest
About an hour before a 7:30am start; previously no consistent time at all
Took a pay cut starting the new job and is waiting for paychecks to normalise

objections.raw_quote: Okay. So I'm going to have to consult my fiance about this before we make that... Yeah, I'd have to consult with her. She's kind of, she's the boss.
objections.rep_response: Ran part of the play — asked whether she knew about the call, offered to bring her on with a precedent ('I spoke to someone literally yesterday, it was the same situation... his wife just asked all the questions that were on her mind'), and pre-framed the discussion by asking what the main obstacle would be. Did not ask the ownership question or offer a deposit

objections.raw_quote: I think it would. Right now, I think it would. With me just starting this job, I took a bit of a pay cut just starting off... But I do think that that would be overextending us at this time.
objections.rep_response: Instead of building a financial picture, descended a price ladder — a three-month tier at $4,000 (about $433/month), then a one-month 'love it or leave it' at $1,200, then Primal University at $200/month

objections.raw_quote: It's still, it's still like, like I said, I just got out of training on, on Wednesday. Right. For this job. So I really got to wait for the, for the paychecks to get where they're supposed to be at.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the delay — 'As I said, that's the plan. We have a plan for the future' — and closed with 'You have my WhatsApp, okay? Anything changes, just hit me up'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Six months spread over 12 at 'a little bit of interest' quoted as 'about 650 bucks a month' — roughly $7,800 against a $6,000 cash price, with no total ever stated. The rep also referenced '975 for the year', implying roughly $11,700 financed against a $9,000 twelve-month price. The improvised three-month tier was quoted at $4,000 spread over 12 months at about $433/month. Credit card described as the usual route, with in-house payment plans 'if necessary'.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: it's called love it or leave it, you come in for a month, 1200 bucks, if you love it, you know, you're in a better financial position in a month, you can continue, if you hate it, no problem, we can part ways as friends

evidence: Declined at every price point offered: six months, the improvised three-month at $4,000 and the $1,200 one-month trial — 'I think we would still be doing too much with those right now'
Explicit statement of inability: 'it's just out the reach right now, out of our range' and 'we're just not financially able to do it yet'
Even the $200/month Primal University placeholder was deferred: 'again, I'd have to talk to her about it... I just need things to clear up here'
No payment, no link, no follow-up call booked; the rep closed with 'You have my WhatsApp, okay? Anything changes, just hit me up'

Counter-evidence, and it is substantial: intent and belief were both high. 'I have no doubt that I'm going to like it when I try it', 'I can justify the cost', 'I really like the six-month option... I think that would be the best for me', and he asked unprompted how to reach the rep with a final answer

Counter-evidence on permanence: he named a future liquidity path (barbershop ownership with an investor) and worried the programme might not still be available when he is ready — this is a deferral driven purely by cash timing
outcome.next_step: Prospect to discuss with his fiancée and revert over WhatsApp; nothing scheduled and no follow-up owned by the rep. Primal University at $200/month left on the table as a placeholder.

notable.note: The price moved $6,000 to $4,000 to $1,200 to $200/month inside roughly four minutes of hesitation, and the three-month and one-month options appear to be discontinued — the rep prefaced them with words to the effect that the company does not do this any more but used to. The financed figure the prospect actually evaluated ($650/month) was never converted into a total, which is $7,800 against a $6,000 cash price. Separately, six months of unresolved shoulder pain was used as the reason to recommend the twelve-month tier, with no question at any point about whether his VA providers had cleared him for loaded kettlebell work. Discovery on this call was the strongest in the batch; the money handling was the weakest.

quality.notes: Inverted from the first line — 'Hello, Tom.' sits under the rep and 'How's it going, Antonio?' under the prospect, when the reverse is true, and the prospect is addressed as Tom and later Anthony. Whole rep passages are labelled Antonio Gatlin II, including 00:17:24 'On the kettlebell side, it's really simple', 00:21:13 the kick-up-the-backside line, 00:22:21 'So these are the three steps, man' and 00:16:18 'you have a pen, paper, laptop?'. The critical passage at 00:35:55-00:35:56, where the discontinued tiers are introduced, is split across both labels and reads as a single rep utterance. Roles were resolved from content throughout. Around 00:28:48-00:29:00 and 00:29:20-00:30:31 the transcription itself garbles badly. No truncation.
